title: Why WW1 Ships Were Painted Like Zebras

scenes.headline: WHY ZEBRA?
scenes.text: Your torpedo target is painted like a giant zebra.

scenes.headline: WHY ZEBRA?
scenes.text: And that's not a mistake. It's the whole plan.
It's nineteen seventeen. U-boats are sinking British ships faster than they can be replaced.

scenes.headline: CAN'T HIDE
scenes.text: You can't hide a ship on the open sea. So a British artist has a strange idea.

scenes.headline: AIM AHEAD
scenes.text: Your torpedo needs time to get there. So you aim where the ship will be, not where it is.

scenes.headline: FEW SECONDS
scenes.text: You judge its speed and heading through a periscope, in seconds.

scenes.headline: WHICH WAY?
scenes.text: But the stripes break up its shape. Which end is the bow? Which way is it turning?

scenes.headline: MISSED
scenes.text: Guess wrong, and your torpedo misses.

scenes.headline: THOUSANDS
scenes.text: Britain painted thousands of ships like this, and America copied the idea.

scenes.headline: NO PROOF?
scenes.text: Did it actually work? A study in nineteen eighteen found no clear proof.

scenes.headline: WHY ZEBRA?
scenes.text: But crews felt safer. Would those stripes fool you?
